blocks.content: A small set of Compose commands covers the overwhelming majority of day-to-day usage: bringing the stack up, tearing it down, watching logs, and getting a shell into a running service.

docker compose up starts every service, attached to your terminal so you see combined logs directly. Adding -d runs the whole stack detached in the background instead, the more common choice once you are past active debugging.

blocks.alt: Foreground for watching logs live, -d for the background

blocks.content:
docker compose up          # foreground, logs streamed to your terminal
docker compose up -d       # detached, runs in the background

code.content:
docker compose up          # foreground, logs streamed to your terminal
docker compose up -d       # detached, runs in the background

codes.bash:
docker compose up          # foreground, logs streamed to your terminal
docker compose up -d       # detached, runs in the background

blocks.content: docker compose down stops and removes every container the stack created, but, as covered in the Volumes topic, named volumes are left intact by default, only -v additionally removes them.

blocks.alt: Containers always removed, volumes only with -v

blocks.content:
docker compose down       # containers gone, named volumes remain
docker compose down -v    # containers and volumes both removed

code.content:
docker compose down       # containers gone, named volumes remain
docker compose down -v    # containers and volumes both removed

codes.bash:
docker compose down       # containers gone, named volumes remain
docker compose down -v    # containers and volumes both removed

blocks.content: 3. Logs and a Shell Into One Service
blocks.text: 3. Logs and a Shell Into One Service

blocks.content: docker compose logs -f follows the combined, interleaved logs of every service at once, useful for watching the whole stack behave together. docker compose exec drops you into a shell inside one specific, already-running service, the Compose equivalent of docker exec.

blocks.alt: Combined logs across every service, or a shell into just one

blocks.content:
docker compose logs -f
docker compose exec app bash

code.content:
docker compose logs -f
docker compose exec app bash

codes.bash:
docker compose logs -f
docker compose exec app bash

blocks.content: For any service defined with build: rather than a plain image:, docker compose build rebuilds its image from the current Dockerfile and source, useful after changing a Dockerfile itself, since up alone does not always rebuild automatically.

blocks.alt: Rebuilding any service backed by a local Dockerfile

blocks.content:
docker compose build
docker compose up -d --build   # rebuild and restart in one step

code.content:
docker compose build
docker compose up -d --build   # rebuild and restart in one step

codes.bash:
docker compose build
docker compose up -d --build   # rebuild and restart in one step

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: up (or up -d) starts the stack, down tears it down while keeping named volumes unless -v is added, this is the core loop you will use constantly.
logs -f and exec cover the two most common debugging needs: watching combined output and getting a shell into one specific service.
